scope: Existing cumulative lists only; no new source nominations or refreshed thread collection

newVetoes.title: The United States of War
newVetoes.author: David Vine
newVetoes.reason: The history is organized as an antiwar argument against the basing system and toward ending permanent war. That sustained political advocacy meets V5; the retained institutional mechanisms still earn counterfactual credit.

newVetoes.title: Progress and Poverty
newVetoes.author: Henry George
newVetoes.reason: The explanation of rents and poverty serves a sustained land-reform program centered on the single tax. Its political-economic prescription meets V5 even where the underlying mechanisms remain useful.

newVetoes.title: The Tyranny of Experts
newVetoes.author: William Easterly
newVetoes.reason: The book advances a rights-centered political program against authoritarian development, rather than only comparing development outcomes. V5 applies to that governing advocacy; the earlier inferential cautions remain.

newVetoes.title: Open Borders
newVetoes.author: Bryan Caplan; Zach Weinersmith
newVetoes.reason: A sustained economic and moral case for opening national borders. The graphic format is nonfiction argument; the central immigration-policy campaign meets V5.

newVetoes.title: The Open Society and Its Enemies
newVetoes.author: Karl R. Popper
newVetoes.reason: The work is a sustained defense of liberal democracy against rival political doctrines. V5 applies to ideological advocacy even when the defended institutions and arguments have substantial intellectual value.

newVetoes.title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
newVetoes.author: Shoshana Zuboff
newVetoes.reason: The diagnosis of digital power is joined to a sustained political demand to resist and replace the surveillance order. This programmatic advocacy meets V5; it does not erase the useful business-model analysis.

newVetoes.title: Stuffed and Starved
newVetoes.author: Raj Patel
newVetoes.reason: The food-system critique advances food sovereignty and political change in the distribution of power over food. This sustained advocacy meets V5; it is not vetoed merely for discussing food or agriculture.

newVetoes.title: Enlightenment Now
newVetoes.author: Steven Pinker
newVetoes.reason: The book explicitly defends reason, science, humanism and progress as a governing social program. The manifesto component meets V5 even though empirical trend evidence retains value.

newVetoes.title: Political Emotions
newVetoes.author: Martha C. Nussbaum
newVetoes.reason: The central project prescribes how liberal societies should cultivate public emotions to sustain their political ideals. This is a normative political program, which V5 now excludes.

newVetoes.title: Animal Liberation
newVetoes.author: Peter Singer
newVetoes.reason: The argument seeks a fundamental change in how people treat animals and supplies the ethical basis for animal liberation. Sustained movement advocacy meets V5 without requiring a finding that its ethics are false.

newVetoes.title: Republic
newVetoes.author: Plato
newVetoes.reason: The dialogue develops and defends a preferred political and educational order. This substantial normative political doctrine meets V5. Its philosophical dialogue form remains eligible nonfiction under the prior format assessment.

newVetoes.title: The Divide
newVetoes.author: Jason Hickel
newVetoes.reason: The account of global inequality supports an explicit program to change the international economic order. Political-economic advocacy is a governing purpose, so V5 applies independently of the unresolved causal disputes.

newVetoes.title: How the World Works
newVetoes.author: Noam Chomsky; edited by Arthur Naiman
newVetoes.reason: The interview collection advances a sustained oppositional political interpretation of power and a case for political action. Its campaign purpose meets V5; useful institutional questions survive only in the counterfactual.

newVetoes.title: Three Guineas
newVetoes.author: Virginia Woolf
newVetoes.reason: The essay is a sustained feminist and antiwar intervention arguing for changes in education, work and public power. Its literary nonfiction form passes the hard exclusions; V5 applies to the advocacy.

newVetoes.title: Gaza Catastrophe
newVetoes.author: Gilbert Achcar
newVetoes.reason: The book presents a sustained political indictment of the forces behind the Gaza war and the international order. V5 applies to that organizing polemic, not simply to its region, author or legal terminology.

newVetoes.title: Poverty, by America
newVetoes.author: Matthew Desmond
newVetoes.reason: The book calls for poverty abolition and asks readers to change policy and their own participation in systems that sustain poverty. This central civil and economic reform campaign meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Silent Spring
newVetoes.author: Rachel Carson
newVetoes.reason: The evidence about pesticide harm supports a sustained intervention to change pesticide use and public policy. This environmental advocacy meets V5; historical importance and reliable risk insights do not override the gate.

newVetoes.title: In Defense of Civilization
newVetoes.author: Michael R. J. Bonner
newVetoes.reason: Historical cases support a prescriptive project of cultural renewal through inherited ideals of order, clarity and beauty. That governing civilizational advocacy meets V5; the judgment does not rest on the author's employment or politics.

newVetoes.title: The Shock Doctrine
newVetoes.author: Naomi Klein
newVetoes.reason: The crisis-capitalism thesis is developed as a sustained political indictment and argument for resistance to the associated economic program. This ideological advocacy meets V5 without needing a fresh V1 finding.

newVetoes.title: Killing Hope
newVetoes.author: William Blum
newVetoes.reason: The case collection is organized as a sustained anti-imperialist indictment of American intervention. V5 applies to that governing political polemic; documentary value remains in the counterfactual.

newVetoes.title: Technofeudalism
newVetoes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
newVetoes.reason: The account of platform rents supports a political argument for moving beyond the present economic order. Its programmatic ideological purpose meets V5; the disputed regime label is not newly treated as proven false.

newVetoes.title: This Life: Secular Faith and Spiritual Freedom
newVetoes.author: Martin Hägglund
newVetoes.reason: The book expressly argues for secular faith and a social order beyond religion and capitalism. That sustained philosophical-political program meets V5.

newVetoes.title: A Sand County Almanac
newVetoes.author: Aldo Leopold
newVetoes.reason: The land ethic asks readers to adopt an ecological moral duty and change human relations with land. This substantial environmental advocacy meets V5 despite the natural-history observations.

newVetoes.title: Just Mercy
newVetoes.author: Bryan Stevenson
newVetoes.reason: The legal memoir makes a sustained case for reforming punishment and racial injustice. Its central civil-justice advocacy meets V5; firsthand evidence and institutional lessons remain credited.

newVetoes.title: Killing the Black Body
newVetoes.author: Dorothy Roberts
newVetoes.reason: Historical and legal analysis serves an explicit reproductive-freedom and racial-justice argument. The sustained civil advocacy meets V5, independently of the quality of its legal history.

newVetoes.title: No god but God
newVetoes.author: Reza Aslan
newVetoes.reason: The historical account also advances a reformist interpretation of Islam and its future. This substantial religious argument meets V5; studying Islamic history alone would not suffice.

newVetoes.title: At the Café
newVetoes.author: Errico Malatesta
newVetoes.reason: The staged conversations explain and defend anarchism. They are expository nonfiction rather than a novel, but the central ideological case directly meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Open Veins of Latin America
newVetoes.author: Eduardo Galeano
newVetoes.reason: The history is organized as an anti-imperialist political-economic indictment with an emancipatory purpose. V5 applies to this sustained ideological argument, not merely to Latin American subject matter.

newVetoes.title: Bullshit Jobs
newVetoes.author: David Graeber
newVetoes.reason: The diagnosis of work serves a sustained political critique of the existing economic order and the case for alternative arrangements. This ideological purpose meets V5; the prior sampling limitations remain in the score.

newVetoes.title: There Are No Accidents
newVetoes.author: Jessie Singer
newVetoes.reason: The analysis of preventable harm is framed as a sustained call to change the political and economic distribution of risk. That civic advocacy meets V5; general safety research alone would not.

newVetoes.title: Washington Bullets
newVetoes.author: Vijay Prashad
newVetoes.reason: A campaigning anti-imperialist account of interventions and resistance. The prior review already identified its campaigning selection; V5 now supplies a category veto without requiring proof of V2.

newVetoes.title: A Life on Our Planet
newVetoes.author: David Attenborough; Jonnie Hughes
newVetoes.reason: The probable nominated work combines testimony with an explicit plan to restore the planet. Environmental campaigning meets V5 if A Life on Our Planet is the intended title; the unresolved alternative Life on Earth does not inherit this decision.

newVetoes.title: The Brutish Museums
newVetoes.author: Dan Hicks
newVetoes.reason: The book argues for restitution and the transformation of museums through a decolonial program. Its manifesto purpose meets V5; provenance scholarship retains counterfactual value.

newVetoes.title: The New Jim Crow
newVetoes.author: Michelle Alexander
newVetoes.reason: The institutional critique supports a sustained movement argument against mass incarceration and racial caste. This civil-justice advocacy meets V5 rather than merely receiving the thematic deduction.

newVetoes.title: Winners Take All
newVetoes.author: Anand Giridharadas
newVetoes.reason: The critique of elite philanthropy seeks a shift of reform power toward democratic collective action. Its sustained political advocacy meets V5; the prior limitations of selected cases remain.

newVetoes.title: God: A Human History
newVetoes.author: Reza Aslan
newVetoes.reason: The publisher states a purpose beyond religious history: developing a more universal spirituality. That constructive spiritual argument meets V5.

newVetoes.title: The Geography of Nowhere
newVetoes.author: James Howard Kunstler
newVetoes.reason: The critique of the American built environment advances a sustained normative case for changing settlement and community design. This political-environmental advocacy meets V5; urban subject matter alone would only trigger T.

newVetoes.title: The God Delusion
newVetoes.author: Richard Dawkins
newVetoes.reason: A sustained argument against religious belief and for abandoning it. V5 applies symmetrically to this worldview advocacy and to religious apologetics; no new factual-error claim is implied.

newVetoes.title: Beggars and Choosers
newVetoes.author: Rickie Solinger
newVetoes.reason: The historical argument advocates reproductive rights and contests the politics of individual choice. Its sustained civil-reform purpose meets V5.

newVetoes.title: My Bondage and My Freedom
newVetoes.author: Frederick Douglass
newVetoes.reason: The autobiography is also a sustained abolitionist intervention against slavery, including arguments directed at public opinion and political change. Its documentary value does not exempt that central civil activism under V5.

newVetoes.title: The Vital Center
newVetoes.author: Arthur M. Schlesinger Jr.
newVetoes.reason: A sustained defense of anti-totalitarian democratic liberalism and its political program. V5 applies to that ideological purpose, even though the position is presented as a center between extremes.

newVetoes.title: America's Deadliest Export: Democracy
newVetoes.author: William Blum
newVetoes.reason: The work is a sustained political polemic against American foreign policy and the claim that it exports democracy. V5 applies to that campaigning purpose without changing the unresolved V1/V2 assessment.

newVetoes.title: The Society of the Spectacle
newVetoes.author: Guy Debord
newVetoes.reason: The theses advance a revolutionary critique of capitalist social relations. Its central Situationist political doctrine meets V5; conceptual influence does not exempt an ideological work.

newVetoes.title: Capital Is Dead
newVetoes.author: McKenzie Wark
newVetoes.reason: The information-economy thesis is used to reframe anticapitalist politics and class struggle. This substantial ideological intervention meets V5; the counterfactual retains the weakness of the regime classification.

newVetoes.title: The Case for God
newVetoes.author: Karen Armstrong
newVetoes.reason: The book argues for a preferred understanding and practice of religion. This religious apologetic purpose meets V5, distinct from a descriptive history of religious institutions.

newVetoes.title: The Omnivore's Deception
newVetoes.author: John Sanbonmatsu
newVetoes.reason: The central argument advocates ending animal exploitation and rejects ethical-meat reform. That sustained animal-liberation program meets V5.

newVetoes.title: An Indigenous Peoples' History of the United States
newVetoes.author: Roxanne Dunbar-Ortiz
newVetoes.reason: The narrative deliberately advances a decolonial political reinterpretation of national history. V5 applies to its sustained ideological intervention; the decision does not follow from the author's identity or the topic alone.

newVetoes.title: Black Feminist Thought
newVetoes.author: Patricia Hill Collins
newVetoes.reason: The book develops Black feminist thought as a framework for empowerment, social justice and action. That constructive ideological and activist purpose meets V5 even though the argument has scholarly standing.

newVetoes.title: Dead Man Walking
newVetoes.author: Helen Prejean
newVetoes.reason: The witness account advances a sustained case against the death penalty. This central civil and moral campaign meets V5; a memoir form does not remove the advocacy.

newVetoes.title: Discourse on Colonialism
newVetoes.author: Aimé Césaire
newVetoes.reason: An explicit anticolonial political polemic. Its central ideological and emancipatory argument directly meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Less Is More
newVetoes.author: Jason Hickel
newVetoes.reason: A sustained case for degrowth and a different political-economic order. Environmental and ideological advocacy meet V5 independently of whether each empirical claim is reliable.

newVetoes.title: Red Star Over the Third World
newVetoes.author: Vijay Prashad
newVetoes.reason: The commemorative argument promotes the emancipatory political legacy of the Russian Revolution. This substantial ideological advocacy meets V5; historical influence alone does not exempt it.

newVetoes.title: Things Hidden Since the Foundation of the World
newVetoes.author: René Girard; with Jean-Michel Oughourlian and Guy Lefort
newVetoes.reason: The theory culminates in a privileged theological account of biblical and Gospel revelation. That constructive religious argument is substantial enough for V5; its comparative concepts retain counterfactual credit.

newVetoes.title: Eating Animals
newVetoes.author: Jonathan Safran Foer
newVetoes.reason: Reporting on food production serves an explicit ethical argument to change participation in animal consumption. This sustained animal-welfare and social advocacy meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Patriot
newVetoes.author: Alexei Navalny
newVetoes.reason: The political memoir and prison testimony explicitly call for continuation of the author's opposition movement. V5 applies to this substantial activist purpose, not merely to political authorship.

newVetoes.title: Tao Te Ching
newVetoes.author: Traditionally Laozi
newVetoes.reason: A foundational Daoist text offering spiritual and governing teachings. V5 applies to that religious-philosophical doctrine; the prior format review found that it is not a procedural manual.

newVetoes.title: The Color of Compromise
newVetoes.author: Jemar Tisby
newVetoes.reason: The historical narrative is addressed to Christians as a call to confront racial injustice and change church practice. Both religious exhortation and civil activism meet V5.

newVetoes.title: Coming Up Short: A Memoir of My America
newVetoes.author: Robert B. Reich
newVetoes.reason: The memoir culminates in an explicit call to recover community and democratic capitalism. That sustained political program meets V5 alongside its personal history.

newVetoes.title: The Autobiography of Malcolm X
newVetoes.author: Malcolm X; Alex Haley
newVetoes.reason: The autobiography advances religious and political commitments through conversion, movement organizing and racial emancipation. This substantial religious and civil-activist purpose meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Ways of Being
newVetoes.author: James Bridle
newVetoes.reason: The discussion of intelligence supports a program for ecological and political coexistence. This central environmental-ideological advocacy meets V5; computation analogies retain limited counterfactual value.

newVetoes.title: How to Sell a Genocide
newVetoes.author: Adam H. Johnson
newVetoes.reason: The media critique is a sustained political intervention against the production of consent for the Gaza war. Its campaigning purpose meets V5; the prior T=0 correction remains because the claimed influence is international.

newVetoes.title: Progress
newVetoes.author: Samuel Miller McDonald
newVetoes.reason: The historical argument explicitly calls for dismantling and rebuilding the meaning of progress to avert ecological destruction. That environmental-political program meets V5.

newVetoes.title: The 1619 Project: A New Origin Story
newVetoes.author: Nikole Hannah-Jones; Caitlin Roper; Ilena Silverman; Jake Silverstein (eds.)
newVetoes.reason: The collection advances a civic reinterpretation of national origins tied to a racial-justice program, including the concluding reparations argument. This substantial ideological and activist purpose meets V5; this judgment concerns the book, not every claim in the earlier newspaper project.

newVetoes.title: Are Prisons Obsolete?
newVetoes.author: Angela Y. Davis
newVetoes.reason: A sustained case for prison abolition. Its explicit civil and political program directly meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Capitalism and Desire
newVetoes.author: Todd McGowan
newVetoes.reason: The publisher states that the psychoanalytic account aims to free readers from attachment to capitalism and open political change. This constructive anticapitalist purpose meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Chasing the Scream
newVetoes.author: Johann Hari
newVetoes.reason: The narrative advocates changing drug prohibition and the institutions of the drug war. This substantial political reform campaign meets V5; the prior evidence limitations remain unchanged.

newVetoes.title: Tyranny, Inc.
newVetoes.author: Sohrab Ahmari
newVetoes.reason: The cases of private coercion support a sustained political argument for a different economic settlement. V5 applies to that ideological program rather than to the author's political affiliation.

newVetoes.title: A People's History of the United States
newVetoes.author: Howard Zinn
newVetoes.reason: The work openly organizes national history around an oppositional politics of popular struggle. Its sustained activist and ideological purpose meets V5; no fresh conclusion about every historical claim is required.

newVetoes.title: Ain't I a Woman: Black Women and Feminism
newVetoes.author: bell hooks
newVetoes.reason: The book advances a Black feminist critique and program for changing feminist politics. This central ideological and civil-activist purpose directly meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Braiding Sweetgrass
newVetoes.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
newVetoes.reason: The essays seek an ecological consciousness grounded in reciprocal obligations with the living world. This central environmental and spiritual exhortation meets V5; botanical observations remain credited.

newVetoes.title: Chavs
newVetoes.author: Owen Jones
newVetoes.reason: A sustained political polemic against the stigmatization of the working class and for a different class politics. This advocacy meets V5, beyond its separate national-history deduction.

newVetoes.title: The Bible
newVetoes.author: Multiple ancient authors
newVetoes.reason: The nominated work is a collection of religious scriptures, not a historical study of them. V5 now applies regardless of canon or translation. The source-8 removal of V1 is not reversed: a category veto does not prove a single empirical argument false.

newVetoes.title: Allow Me to Retort
newVetoes.author: Elie Mystal
newVetoes.reason: The constitutional argument is a sustained political and racial-justice polemic. V5 applies to its advocacy purpose; the previous lack of a proven V2 defect no longer preserves eligibility.

newVetoes.title: In the Spirit of Crazy Horse
newVetoes.author: Peter Matthiessen
newVetoes.reason: The account advances the cause of the American Indian Movement and a contested legal-defense campaign. This substantial civil and political advocacy meets V5; surviving litigation is not treated as proof of its claims.

newVetoes.title: Animal, Vegetable, Miracle
newVetoes.author: Barbara Kingsolver; Steven L. Hopp; Camille Kingsolver
newVetoes.reason: The household narrative is used to advocate local food production and changed consumption as an environmental and social response. That sustained campaign meets V5; it is not primarily a recipe manual.

newVetoes.title: Cutting Through Spiritual Materialism
newVetoes.author: Chögyam Trungpa
newVetoes.reason: The lectures teach Buddhist spiritual understanding and practice. Their religious purpose meets V5 even where self-deception observations have secular uses; the work is not primarily an exercise manual.

newVetoes.title: Between the World and Me
newVetoes.author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
newVetoes.reason: The letter is also a sustained intervention in racial politics, arguing for changed understanding of the American social order. Its substantial civil-advocacy purpose meets V5; memoir form and prose quality do not exempt it.

newVetoes.title: Abolish Rent
newVetoes.author: Tracy Rosenthal; Leonardo Vilchis
newVetoes.reason: An explicit tenant-movement manifesto for ending rent-based domination. V5 applies to the political program. Analysis and movement reporting are the main structure, so it is not reclassified as a procedural manual.

newVetoes.title: Awareness
newVetoes.author: Anthony de Mello
newVetoes.reason: Spiritual talks aim at awakening and release from attachment. This religious-spiritual teaching meets V5, while the discursive format does not by itself establish a procedural hard exclusion.

newVetoes.title: How to Do Nothing
newVetoes.author: Jenny Odell
newVetoes.reason: The critique of the attention economy is a sustained call for political and ecological resistance through redirected attention. This programmatic advocacy meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Answer to Job
newVetoes.author: C. G. Jung
newVetoes.reason: The essay develops a constructive theological interpretation of God, revelation and moral transformation. V5 applies to that substantial religious argument; it is not classified as fiction or rejected merely for analyzing an old text.

newVetoes.title: Who Stole Feminism?
newVetoes.author: Christina Hoff Sommers
newVetoes.reason: The book is a sustained intervention in feminist politics that defends one version of feminism against another. V5 applies to ideological advocacy on either side; the earlier uncertainty about V2 remains separate.

newVetoes.title: Koba the Dread
newVetoes.author: Martin Amis
newVetoes.reason: The literary-historical essay is a sustained political polemic against communist apologetics. This ideological intervention meets V5; criticism of state violence is not newly treated as a factual error.

newVetoes.title: Lordship and Liberation in Palestine-Israel
newVetoes.author: Muhannad Ayyash
newVetoes.reason: The book explicitly argues for decolonial sovereignty as the political alternative to colonial modernity. That constructive liberation program meets V5; proof of suppressed counterexamples under V2 is unnecessary.

newVetoes.title: Whitewalling
newVetoes.author: Aruna D'Souza
newVetoes.reason: The museum controversies support a sustained antiracist intervention in art institutions. Its civil-activist purpose meets V5; the small sample and prior limits remain in the counterfactual.

newVetoes.title: Virtue Hoarders
newVetoes.author: Catherine Liu
newVetoes.reason: An explicit political polemic against the professional-managerial class and its claimed virtue. The sustained ideological intervention meets V5 despite its small institutional payload.

newVetoes.title: Assata
newVetoes.author: Assata Shakur
newVetoes.reason: The participant account advances a revolutionary political cause and defense of a movement. That substantial activist purpose meets V5; the decision does not resolve contested allegations about the author.

newVetoes.title: Columbus and Other Cannibals
newVetoes.author: Jack D. Forbes
newVetoes.reason: The colonial critique advances an Indigenous ethical-political worldview against exploitation. This sustained ideological and decolonial program meets V5, without treating cultural provenance itself as a defect.

newVetoes.title: Desert Solitaire
newVetoes.author: Edward Abbey
newVetoes.reason: The essays make wilderness defense and opposition to industrial tourism a substantial organizing purpose. Environmental advocacy therefore meets V5; literary observations do not override it.

newVetoes.title: The End of America
newVetoes.author: Naomi Wolf
newVetoes.reason: A sustained call to political action against authoritarian change in the United States. This civic manifesto meets V5 without needing to classify every comparison or prediction as false.

newVetoes.title: Being Ecological
newVetoes.author: Timothy Morton
newVetoes.reason: The work argues for adopting an ecological way of understanding and inhabiting the world. That constructive environmental philosophy and advocacy meets V5.

newVetoes.title: So You Want to Talk About Race
newVetoes.author: Ijeoma Oluo
newVetoes.reason: The explanatory chapters advocate antiracist understanding and action. V5 applies to the civil-activist purpose. The mixed discussion-and-advice structure is not established as primarily a procedural manual, so hard exclusion 2 is not asserted.

newVetoes.title: Sacred Economics
newVetoes.author: Charles Eisenstein
newVetoes.reason: The monetary critique advances a spiritual and ecological program of gift exchange, commons and economic transformation. That sustained ideological-spiritual advocacy meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Jacob Hamblin: The Peacemaker
newVetoes.author: Pearson H. Corbett
newVetoes.reason: The biography is a faith-centered account of a Mormon missionary, including spiritual authority and miracle narratives. Its religious purpose meets V5; this is the Corbett biography, not another work about Hamblin.

newVetoes.title: Soul on Ice
newVetoes.author: Eldridge Cleaver
newVetoes.reason: The essays articulate and advance a revolutionary racial-political worldview. This sustained ideological intervention meets V5, beyond the thematic deduction.

newVetoes.title: Whakapohane
newVetoes.author: Dun Mihaka; Diane Prince
newVetoes.reason: The account defends a political protest and frames the associated prosecution as a struggle against state authority. Its participant activist purpose meets V5; the 1984 work and expanded later version remain the same qualified source entry.

newVetoes.title: Food of the Gods
newVetoes.author: Terence McKenna
newVetoes.reason: The history of psychoactive plants supports a call to recover shamanic and psychedelic spirituality as a response to modern culture. This substantial spiritual-cultural program meets V5; the evolutionary claims retain their prior low evidential credit.

newVetoes.title: Heroes: Mass Murder and Suicide
newVetoes.author: Franco Berardi
newVetoes.reason: The cases are organized into an anticapitalist political diagnosis and appeal to recover social alternatives. This ideological intervention meets V5; the counterfactual keeps the untested causal links and T=-10.

newVetoes.title: The Tao of Wu
newVetoes.author: RZA
newVetoes.reason: The autobiography conveys a sustained spiritual teaching drawn from the author's religious and philosophical commitments. V5 applies to that substantial teaching, in addition to its already penalized celebrity context.

newVetoes.title: This One Wild and Precious Life
newVetoes.author: Sarah Wilson
newVetoes.reason: The personal narrative calls for collective ecological and social change, grounded partly in spiritual renewal. This environmental-activist purpose meets V5.

newVetoes.title: Emptiness Dancing
newVetoes.author: Adyashanti
newVetoes.reason: The work teaches spiritual awakening and a view of ultimate reality. That religious-spiritual purpose directly meets V5; the retained format assessment treats it as discursive teaching rather than a technical practice manual.

newVetoes.title: The Book of Invasions (Lebor Gabála Érenn)
newVetoes.author: Anonymous; R. A. S. Macalister, ed./trans.
newVetoes.reason: The medieval narrative constructs a Christian universal and national origin account. V5 applies to that religious-ideological purpose. It remains a historical primary text rather than being relabeled a modern novel; the narrative text, not a modern scholarly apparatus alone, is the nominated work.

amendedVetoes.title: Capital / Das Kapital
amendedVetoes.author: Karl Marx
amendedVetoes.reason: The sustained critique of capitalism is also a foundational socialist political-economic argument. This ideological purpose independently meets V5. The existing V1 assessment remains at moderate confidence.

amendedVetoes.title: The Communist Manifesto
amendedVetoes.author: Karl Marx; Friedrich Engels
amendedVetoes.reason: An explicit communist political manifesto. V5 applies independently of the existing V1 and V2 judgments, whose prior confidence remains moderate.

amendedVetoes.title: The Matter with Things
amendedVetoes.author: Iain McGilchrist
amendedVetoes.reason: The work uses its account of mind and reality to defend a substantial sacred and divine worldview. That constructive spiritual-metaphysical purpose meets V5; the existing V1 inference concern remains unchanged.

amendedVetoes.title: Human Smoke
amendedVetoes.author: Nicholson Baker
amendedVetoes.reason: The selected historical fragments serve a sustained pacifist political argument about the Second World War. V5 independently applies to the antiwar polemic; the existing V1 concern about inference remains.

amendedVetoes.title: The New Left / The Return of the Primitive
amendedVetoes.author: Ayn Rand; Peter Schwartz (expanded edition)
amendedVetoes.reason: The essays defend Objectivist political values against opposing cultural and environmental programs. The sustained ideological polemic directly meets V5, alongside the existing V2 judgment.

amendedVetoes.title: The Power of Now
amendedVetoes.author: Eckhart Tolle
amendedVetoes.reason: Spiritual awakening and liberation from the ego are the central teachings. V5 applies to this religious-spiritual account independently of the existing V1 judgment.

amendedVetoes.title: Autobiography of a Yogi
amendedVetoes.author: Paramahansa Yogananda
amendedVetoes.reason: The memoir teaches and promotes a religious path through its spiritual lineage and miracle accounts. V5 applies independently of the existing high-confidence V1 judgment.

amendedVetoes.title: The Book of Enoch
amendedVetoes.author: Multiple ancient authors (1 Enoch assumed)
amendedVetoes.reason: For the assumed work, 1 Enoch, the religious and apocalyptic character directly meets V5. Identity uncertainty remains; this is not a resolution among 1, 2 and 3 Enoch. The prior V1 judgment is retained conditionally.

amendedVetoes.title: A New Earth
amendedVetoes.author: Eckhart Tolle
amendedVetoes.reason: The book promotes spiritual transformation and awakening as its central purpose. V5 applies independently of the existing V1 concerns.

amendedVetoes.title: Expecting Adam
amendedVetoes.author: Martha Beck
amendedVetoes.reason: Miraculous guidance and spiritual transformation organize the memoir. That substantial religious purpose meets V5 independently of the existing V1 judgment.

amendedVetoes.title: The Biology of Belief
